214.title: SHORTEST PALINDROME  (String Matching)
214.script:
# PHASE 1 — CLARIFY
# "Add minimum characters to the front of s to make it a palindrome. Right?"
# "s='aacecaaa'→'aaacecaaa' ✓  s='abcd'→'dcbabcd' ✓"
class _214_ShortestPalindrome_Brute:
    def shortestPalindrome(self,s):
        n=len(s)
        for i in range(n,-1,-1):
            if s[:i]==s[:i][::-1]: return s[i:][::-1]+s
        return ''
class _214_ShortestPalindrome:
    def shortestPalindrome(self,s):
        # KMP on s+'#'+reverse(s) to find longest palindrome prefix
        t=s+'#'+s[::-1]; n=len(t)
        fail=[0]*n
        for i in range(1,n):
            j=fail[i-1]
            while j>0 and t[i]!=t[j]: j=fail[j-1]
            if t[i]==t[j]: j+=1
            fail[i]=j
        longest_pal_prefix=fail[-1]
        return s[longest_pal_prefix:][::-1]+s
# KMP failure function on s+'#'+rev(s). Longest prefix of s that's also a palindrome. O(n). Space O(n).
# Follow-up: Longest Palindromic Prefix — return the palindrome itself.
# Follow-up: Shortest Palindrome by Adding to End — reverse the problem.

1044.title: LONGEST DUPLICATE SUBSTRING  (String Matching)
1044.script:
# PHASE 1 — CLARIFY
# "Find the longest duplicate substring (appearing at least twice). Return '' if none. Right?"
# "s='banana'→'ana' ✓  s='abcd'→'' ✓"
class _1044_LongestDuplicateSubstring_Brute:
    def longestDupSubstr(self,s):
        n=len(s)
        def has_dup(length):
            seen=set()
            for i in range(n-length+1):
                sub=s[i:i+length]
                if sub in seen: return sub
                seen.add(sub)
            return None
        lo,hi=1,n-1; result=''
        while lo<=hi:
            mid=(lo+hi)//2
            found=has_dup(mid)
            if found: result=found; lo=mid+1
            else: hi=mid-1
        return result
class _1044_LongestDuplicateSubstring:
    def longestDupSubstr(self,s):
        # Binary search + rolling hash
        MOD=2**61-1; BASE=31; n=len(s)
        def check(length):
            h=0; pw=pow(BASE,length,MOD)
            seen=set()
            for i in range(length): h=(h*BASE+ord(s[i]))%MOD
            seen.add((h,s[:length])); 
            for i in range(1,n-length+1):
                h=(h*BASE-ord(s[i-1])*pw+ord(s[i+length-1]))%MOD
                key=(h,s[i:i+length])
                if key in seen: return s[i:i+length]
                seen.add(key)
            return None
        lo,hi=1,n-1; result=''
        while lo<=hi:
            mid=(lo+hi)//2
            found=check(mid)
            if found: result=found; lo=mid+1
            else: hi=mid-1
        return result
# Binary search on length + rolling hash. O(n log n). Space O(n).
# Suffix array approach: O(n log²n) build, O(n) to find answer.
# Follow-up: number of distinct substrings — n*(n+1)/2 - sum(LCP array).

1392.title: LONGEST HAPPY PREFIX  (String Matching)
1392.script:
# PHASE 1 — CLARIFY
# "A 'happy prefix' is a non-empty prefix of s that is also a suffix (but not the whole string).
#  Return the longest one or '' if none. Right?"
# "s='level'→'l' ✓  s='ababab'→'abab' ✓"
class _1392_LongestHappyPrefix_Brute:
    def longestPrefix(self,s):
        n=len(s)
        for length in range(n-1,0,-1):
            if s[:length]==s[n-length:]: return s[:length]
        return ''
class _1392_LongestHappyPrefix:
    def longestPrefix(self,s):
        # KMP failure function: fail[i] = length of longest proper prefix=suffix of s[:i+1]
        n=len(s); fail=[0]*n
        for i in range(1,n):
            j=fail[i-1]
            while j>0 and s[i]!=s[j]: j=fail[j-1]
            if s[i]==s[j]: j+=1
            fail[i]=j
        return s[:fail[-1]]
# KMP failure function: last value = length of longest proper prefix that is also suffix. O(n).
# Follow-up: Shortest Palindrome (LC 214) — uses same KMP trick.
# Follow-up: count all happy prefixes — positions in fail array where fail[i]>0.

699.title: FALLING SQUARES  (Binary Indexed Tree / Segment Tree)
699.script:
# PHASE 1 — CLARIFY
# "Squares fall onto x-axis. Each square settles on the highest stack. Return max height after each drop. Right?"
# "positions=[[1,2],[2,3],[6,1]]→[2,5,5] ✓"
class _699_FallingSquares_Brute:
    def fallingSquares(self,positions):
        heights=[0]*len(positions); result=[]
        for i,(left,size) in enumerate(positions):
            right=left+size; heights[i]=size
            for j in range(i):
                l2,s2=positions[j]; r2=l2+s2
                if l2<right and left<r2: heights[i]=max(heights[i],heights[j]+size)
            result.append(max(heights[:i+1]))
        return result
class _699_FallingSquares:
    def fallingSquares(self,positions):
        # Coordinate compress + segment tree for range max query
        coords=sorted(set(x for l,s in positions for x in [l,l+s]))
        ci={c:i for i,c in enumerate(coords)}; n=len(coords)
        tree=[0]*(4*n)
        def update(node,lo,hi,l,r,val):
            if r<=lo or hi<=l: return
            if l<=lo and hi<=r: tree[node]=max(tree[node],val); return
            mid=(lo+hi)//2
            update(2*node,lo,mid,l,r,val); update(2*node+1,mid,hi,l,r,val)
        def query(node,lo,hi,l,r):
            if r<=lo or hi<=l: return 0
            if l<=lo and hi<=r: return tree[node]
            mid=(lo+hi)//2
            return max(query(2*node,lo,mid,l,r),query(2*node+1,mid,hi,l,r))
        result=[]; mx=0
        for left,size in positions:
            right=left+size; l,r=ci[left],ci[right]
            h=query(1,0,n,l,r)+size; update(1,0,n,l,r,h); mx=max(mx,h); result.append(mx)
        return result
# Segment tree with lazy max. O(n log n). Space O(n).
# Follow-up: if squares can be removed — harder, need actual height tracking per position.
# Follow-up: Range Module (LC 715) — track covered intervals instead of heights.
